title: SCHEMBL4796824: a multifaceted antitumor agent targeting microtubule dynamics, DNA damage, and Wnt/beta-catenin signaling in ovarian cancer cells.
authors: Ma, Chaoyue; Ding, XiaoFei; Wang, Boze; Zhu, Xinya; Zhang, Yijia; Ding, Meidan; Ding, Xiaoxiao; Zhou, Jun; Zuo, Daiying; Huang, Yingrui; Ma, Yongmin; Chen, Guang
one_liner_zh: 该文研究小分子抗肿瘤药物对微管、DNA损伤及Wnt信号通路的影响，仅涉及分子对接预测与CTNNB1的潜在结合，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合体系，且无AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: SCHEMBL4796824, a BPR0L075 derivative with antitumor properties, targets tubulin's colchicine binding site and induces DNA damage response in ovarian cancer. Cell counting kit-8 (CCK-8) assay confirmed its anti-proliferative effects, while wound healing and transwell assays demonstrated inhibition of migration and invasion. Flow cytometry showed G2 phase arrest. Molecular docking and immunofluorescence revealed microtubule depolymerization via tubulin binding, analogy with BPR0L075. Real-time qPCR and western blot analysis indicated activation of ATM/Chk2 and ATR/Chk1 pathways by SCHEMBL4796824. Senescence-associated-beta-galactosidase (SA-beta-gal) staining showed senescence induction. Molecular docking studies suggested potential interaction with CTNNB1. Crucially, functional assays demonstrated inhibition of the Wnt/beta-catenin pathway, as evidenced by downregulation of beta-catenin and c-MYC. The beta-catenin agonist reversed SCHEMBL4796824-induced DNA damage and senescence, establishing a causal link to the observed phenotypes. Notably, these effects were more pronounced in c-MYC amplified SK-OV-3 cells. In summary, SCHEMBL4796824 disrupts the canonical Wnt/beta-catenin signaling, inducing DNA damage, and inhibits the Wnt/beta-catenin/c-MYC axis, triggering cellular senescence in a pathway-dependent manner, hinting at a novel therapeutic approach.
abstract_zh: SCHEMBL4796824，一种具有抗肿瘤特性的BPR0L075衍生物，靶向微管蛋白的秋水仙碱结合位点并在卵巢癌中诱导DNA损伤反应。细胞计数试剂盒-8（CCK-8）实验确认了其抗增殖作用，而伤口愈合和transwell实验表明其抑制迁移和侵袭。流式细胞术显示G2期阻滞。分子对接和免疫荧光揭示通过微管蛋白结合导致微管解聚，与BPR0L075类似。实时qPCR和western blot分析表明SCHEMBL4796824激活ATM/Chk2和ATR/Chk1通路。衰老相关β-半乳糖苷酶（SA-beta-gal）染色显示诱导衰老。分子对接研究提示可能与CTNNB1存在潜在相互作用。关键的是，功能实验证明抑制Wnt/β-catenin通路，表现为β-catenin和c-MYC下调。β-catenin激动剂逆转了SCHEMBL4796824诱导的DNA损伤和衰老，确立了与观察表型的因果关系。值得注意的是，这些效应在c-MYC扩增的SK-OV-3细胞中更为显著。总之，SCHEMBL4796824破坏经典Wnt/β-catenin信号传导，诱导DNA损伤，并抑制Wnt/β-catenin/c-MYC轴，以通路依赖性方式触发细胞衰老，提示一种新的治疗策略。
